BiblicalUsage: This word occurs once, in Genesis 41:43, when Pharaoh sets Joseph over Egypt: 'he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.' It is the herald's cry — the command for all Egypt to kneel as Joseph passes.
TheologicalSignificance: One cry, and a slave becomes a ruler — ‘Bow the knee’ — and I believe the word points further than Joseph, to the day when every knee will bow.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
